subject: COBOL character repertoire
notes: kb/Work PB1965 (w1047a): b) reaches the word tables outside the compiler and frontend: final sigma keeps its own key at 2023 (E.2 item 14) in C# identifiers and EXTERNAL identities, and below 2023 folds to sigma (two METHOD-IDs X<final sigma> and X<sigma> are one name, COBOL0822). kb/Work PB4420 (owner decision 2026-11-01, follow GnuCOBOL): b) names the corresponding lowercase EXTENDED letter, so the fold applies an Annex C pair only when both letters are basic or both extended; the pairs that cross (0130,0069), (212A,006B) and, in the 2002/2014 table, (0131,0069) are transcribed from the standard and NOT applied (CobolNames.NotApplied, derived by gen_annex_bc.py), so a word spelled with U+0130 or the Kelvin sign is a user-defined word of its own, no reserved word and no synonym of one, and CUSTOMER-<U+0130>D and CUSTOMER-ID are two names. retired-witness: conformance:cases/8.1.3-COBOL-character-repertoire/pb1965-kelvin-spelled-reserved-word (kb/Work PB4420 (owner decision 2026-11-01): the Kelvin sign pairs with a BASIC letter, which 8.1.3.2 4) b) (corresponding lowercase EXTENDED letter) does not reach, so the fold does not apply (212A,006B) and a word spelled with it is no reserved word; the golden is now pb4420-kelvin-spelled-key-is-a-user-word)
